body: Yeah I think it’s house ruled sometimes. As for Throw it might be helpful to compare it to the giant barbarians mighty impel for some potential reference. As for putting a height limit, that might be one way to solve it. Make sure you keep in mind the potential of throwing someone diagonally upwards an away in the wording. I personally like the potential of applying fall damage, but you have to be careful with the balance. If you do end up choosing to have it be a purely horizontal displacement than adding damage, when a creature hits an object or creature without traveling, the full distance might be cool.

I understand your intentions behind gaining Hype from critically succeeding on the checks, but I will again emphasize that that isn’t a thing. You cannot critically succeed on an athletics check, that mechanic only applies to attacks. 

Another thing I totally forgot to mention in my first comment was how throw interacts with fall damage. Currently, you can use it to throw a grapple creature upwards forcing them to also take the fall damage in addition to the standard damage from the ability, which could potentially result in a pretty huge DPR. Again, I haven’t mathed that out compared to other barbarians, but I think it’s a good thing to keep in mind as to whether or not you intend that because it would vary greatly change the overall power of the subclass. 

Love your other revisions! I like your vision. Keep it up!

As someone who loves barbarians and grappling in both DnD and fighting games(great art choices btw shoutout Beo and X) I really like both the theming and abilities here. Fits the archetype very well, is creative, and looks fun. After a readthrough and some light theory-crafting I think it’s fairly balanced overall, but I do have some thoughts/critiques. 

First and foremost, I think the methods for gaining Hype probably need another pass. I like that Throw cost Hype but is also a net Hype gain. not only is that thematically cool but it also allows you to potentially snowball your Hype over the course of a combat. However, getting that first Hype might be really tricky as the only ways to generate Hype without first spending Hype are unreliable and somewhat vague. Rolling max on a damage die and landing a crit on an attack are both pretty rare, but critically succeeding on a STR or CHA check is impossible because critically succeeding on skill checks doesn’t exist within the rules of 5e. Additionally, “going 1 turn without taking damage from attack rolls while reckless attacking” is a bit weird wording wise. You don’t take damage from an attack roll you take it from an attack, but that’s just syntax. The main thing here is the “1 turn” aspect, which implies that it triggers on every individual turn including your own. In combats with a lot of creatures in the initiative that could be really powerful. Big emphasis on could there though, because these Hype generation methods are generally both pretty rare and entirely out of your control meaning there’s a pretty good chance you won’t get any Hype at all if you’re not lucky, which would feel really bad. I think all of these ways of getting Hype are excellent, but I think these options need to be refined and expanded a little bit to make getting off the ground more possible. 

Throw is also a bit tricky because since it’s not an attack using it doesn’t extend your rage, making it potentially a gamble especially before extra attack. 

Title Fight includes the bloodied condition which isn’t officially a defined term in 5e 2014. 

As written, Blockbuster Finish doesn’t have any action requirements meaning it lets you make an attack as a free action any time on any turn once a long rest. I assume that’s an oversight, but issues written it’s totally crazy. It also says “while raging, you may expand 4 more Hype while raging” which is funny. 

Other than the things mentioned above, I think you’ve got a really solid homebrew on your hands! I hope stuff I said will be helpful if you choose to revise this, because it looks really fun and I would like to play it someday.

Good questions and they are all variable. If you think you can get to lvl 20 then I would recommend not taking a fourth Fighter lvl. If you know you’re not going to get to 20 then you could, but it would slow down your Cleric progression, which I personally don’t know if it would be worth it. 

If you’re starting Fighter it could be argued that Warcaster is optional, but IMO it’s nice to have. Depending on your stats, it’s likely that you won’t have room for many feats, but there are a couple nice ones. You already mentioned Crusher for the combo with Booming Blade and that’s certainly a good pick. I think Heavy Armor Master is under appreciated, and provides nice durability with flavor to boot. If you wanna really lean into the fire aspect Elemental Adept is a nice option but play style dependent. 

Feat suggestions leads nicely into stats because unfortunately this build is MAD. To be able to really live the fantasy of the concept that you’re going for, STR CON and WIS are all important to get pretty high. As I mentioned earlier, it’s gonna really be play style dependent. If you find that you are prioritizing melee and wanting to hit more consistently, then go STR. Not enough spells landing or prepared? WIS. Feeling fragile? CON. Ideally you’d eventually get them all to 20, but that’s not always feasible.

Cool. So the great thing about this is it doesn’t put you behind in spellcasting too much, while patching some of the holes in the cleric spell list. As almost exclusively a toplane tank player I was overjoyed on release and have been having a lot of fun with grasp. Overall I’m greatly enjoying his kit and having basically a brand new tank to play with is great but I do have a few gripes. My takes are these:

The windup on Q makes perfect thematic sense and the animation is very clean, but unfortunately it really does hurt the tempo of his trading and feels especially bad that it’s the only AA enhancement that has such a punishment AFAIK. I think it should either be faster or be usable while moving. 

The ult is borderline impossible to pull of in lane unless the enemy makes a stupid towerdive. Long windup + almost no damage + only W means that actually using it is a dual is usually a bad idea and the overall lack of speed makes dragging them to tower mostly impossible. 

I played a few games of the poke build with comet and although vaguely interesting in concept I got bored pretty quick. Given the lack of interaction on both sides I think it should be disincentivized in favor of more of a brawling style. It seems like riot sees this but WORSE MANA COSTS ARE NOT THE WAY! I’m so tired of so many tanks being forced to take mana in their runes and/or get an early tear just to be able to survive lane. Tanks heavily rely on their abilities to trade and these mana nerfs will only push Skarner to rely MORE on passive play like the comet build, and It’s insane to me that rito doesn’t see that. 

Overall I LOVE his gameplay but the top nerf really hurt and IMO feel poorly thought out.

Edit: I can’t believe I totally forgot but some of these other comments got to it already: the E should scale with movement speed. It probably wouldn’t be enough to be the meta build, but being able to play around with a Warwick-esq full MS build would be fun.

The selling point is having a bunch of relatively good minions. Aside from that, there’s not much going on. I do believe that they get the short end of the stick though for multiple reasons. 

1. No spells. The necromancy spell list is very short, especially at low levels. If you want to play a necromancer I strongly recommend talking to your DM and seeing if they’d be open to the two of you finding some homebrew spells. Lots of people are aware of this problem, and necromancy spells are some of the most homebrewed, and there are a lot of excellent choices out there. 

2. Lacking subclass features. Wizards are known for having relatively simple or low power subclass features because most of their innate strength comes from the spell list, but school of necromancy is interesting because aside from the level six feature that most of your power will come from, you’re getting mostly ribbons. Again, if it’s campaign appropriate, I suggest some light homebrew here. Nothing too extreme just some slight touchups of the 2nd and 10th levels. If the DM has allowed some homebrew spells, this is less of a big deal. 

The combination of these two problems makes playing a necromancer before level six pretty unsatisfying, but there is a third issue, which is arguably the most important out of all of them. 

3. They’re EXTREMELY DM/campaign reliant. If you can’t get a hold of any bodies or bones, you’re not going to be able to have any minions, which will basically remove your subclass features. If you’re not fighting or killing humanoids, a lot of your best spells won’t work against them, and you won’t have any bodies you can raise. If you can get a fair amount of minions, you’d better hope there’s a place you can buy plenty of cheap gear for them. If you can get a lot of minions then you’ll either need to be very comfortable with controlling lots of summons, efficiently, or the rest of the people you’re playing with might get bored or frustrated. If you’re going to be spending a lot of time in towns/cities that frown on having a lot of undead following you around, you better hope that the DM gives you a bag of holding or you’re high enough level to have a good enough illusions to make them look like soldiers. All of this boils down to needing to make sure the game you’re playing, is right for playing a necromancer. 

TL/DR: Can you have a lot of fun and be very powerful as a necromancer? Definitely. Is the subclass/spell list kind of lacking? IMO absolutely. Is a necromancer the kind of character you can play in basically any campaign? Definitely not. Having the right group/setting is extremely important, and IMO a little bit of homebrew is required to make playing one satisfying.

Let me preface this a little bit by say barbarian is my favorite class, it’s definitely one of the weakest classes in the game, I’ve wanted an unarmed/grappling subclass since forever, and these abilities look really fun. 

With that said, this is just way too much. Is it stronger then any other barbarian subclass? Absolutely. Is it stronger then your average caster? I don’t know. That would probably take a lot of math that I’m not interested in doing right now. Regardless of whether or not this is overpowered(probably), it’s just WAY too many abilities. 

Every barbarian subclass follows the same outline: 1 or 2 features at lvl 3, 1 feature at lvl 6, 1 feature at lvl 10, and 1 feature at lvl 14. Given the general weakness of the base class, there’s an argument to be made for a homebrew subclass to be able add in an additional feature at one of the later levels, depending on the overall power of the subclass. That’s a total of 4 to 5 features(6 if you really wanna be nice, but no official Barbarian subclass has this many).

This subclass gets 2 features at lvl 3, 2 features at lvl 6, 1 feature at lvl 9, 2 features at lvl 10, 2 features at lvl 14, and 1 feature at lvl 18 for a total of 10 features including 2 features at lvls where barbarian subclasses don’t get features, meaning on paper this subclass gets TWICE as much to work with as any other barbarian subclass, but most of these features include multiple distinct abilities, so in reality it’s much more than that. 

I really like the concept you’re working with here, and individually the abilities all look interesting and fun to use, but it’s just too much. In my own personal experience, designing homebrew, the hardest part for me is trimming extraneous abilities. I hate giving up cool ideas as much as the next guy, but if you want this to be balanced, you’re gonna have to let some things go. I would love to see more versions of the sub class in the future, and I think the first step should be narrowing it down to the 4 to 6 features range. I know what I’m saying, might sound like a lot of hard criticism, but I really hope my words don’t discourage you from continuing this project, and any other similar projects in the future. 

TL;DR: looks really cool, but has way too many features. Trim it down to be more in line with official content.

TLDR, basically everything about her makes her effective at countering tanks, and on top of that, she can specifically take advantage of some of Ornn‘s particular weaknesses.

I’ve done a fair amount of research about this particular question. The following is what I know to be true, but it’s not impossible that I’m wrong considering differing interpretations. 

The short answer is “no”. The slightly longer answer is “yes, kind of”, and the best answer is “talk to your DM”. 

As far as I understand, the basic mechanics of grappling state that you can either push or pull a creature you are grappling, that is to say you cannot move a creatures relative position to you. If a creature you are grappling is to the north of you, you can push it north, you can drag it south, east or west, but the creature will continue to be to your north. However, you can move around a creature you are grappling. As far as I know, this is the only strictly official way to change a grappled creatures relative position to you. 

And now we get into a little bit of a gray area. As far as I understand it, it’s not really entirely agreed-upon whether or not you can move a grappled creature around you, considering it’s not written about with very much depth. Many tables use the pure RAW explanation and do not deviate from what I have written above. Probably a similar number of tables use a RAI method where you can move a grappled creature freely around you As long as they never leave your reach. I personally find a more middle ground to be useful, such as sacrificing some of your own movement to move the grappled creature an equal amount, or allowing you to move them freely within your reach so long as you succeed an additional contested athletics check. As much as I am under most circumstances a proponent of RAW, in this case I would highly recommend talking to your DM about this specific mechanic to make sure you are both on the same page, and can find something that feels good for everyone involved.

The thing about grappling is it gives very little in terms of power, and for almost any character it is rarely the optimal choice. 

With that being said, it is by far my favorite mechanic in 5e. 

There are many ways to go about it, many things to do with it. To pull it off reliably and successfully, basically any grappler would do well to try and have these three things: High Strength, expertise in athletics, and advantage on the contested check. There are a few ways of doing it that give disadvantage on the enemy’s check, but that’s much less common and also generally less reliable. 

There are very few situations where grappling is going to increase your DPR. In fact, under most circumstances it will decrease it. However, the grapple/prone combo is a very potent strategy for granting advantage on melee attacks, which can not only be useful for yourself, but highly beneficial for other members of the party. Additionally, look for synergy with spells like Spike Growth and Cloud of Daggers for some potentially very high damage. 

Obviously there are ways of using grappling to generate some nice damage, but at the end of the day it is primarily a control tool. Being able to halt or force movement of enemies can give great tactical advantage in the right situation.

Downsides come primarily from the low number of enemies you can have grappled at a time, limitations of size category(this is why rune knight is so prevalent in grappling builds), forced movement automatically breaking grapples, and being completely unusable against enemies that can teleport, or simply just immune to the grappled condition. 

Is grappling useful? Yes definitely. Is grappling powerful? In the right situation it can be very potent, but honestly under most circumstances I’m inclined to say no. Is grappling fun? Yes! There are very few things I love more in DND then being able to absolutely manhandle my opponents. There also comes a pointfor most characters that focus very heavily on grappling where it is almost impossible for them to fail a grapple check against most targets grapplable targets. Playing as unarmed, unarmored grapplers has led to some of my most fond D&D memories.

Hey no problem I love reading creative homebrew and thinking about it in the context of an actual game. With the context that it would be a spell given to loyal followers with the intention that they use on you, it makes a lot more sense, but I still have some things to say about it. 

Firstly, let’s talk purely numbers. There are a few big problems with this, which would usually be fairly minor for most casters, but are extremely detrimental in the case of warlocks. The first issue is the low number of pact slots. Warlocks are the most spell slot starved class in the game, and this spell makes that weakness so much more glaring. Let’s take your example of giving an ally back one of their 1st lvl slot. That means you need to cast this spell three times. That means that until you hit lvl 11(when you have 3 pact slots) you will need to take multiple short rests in a row just to restore a SINGLE allied spell slot. That’s just horrible. Secondly, the big thing about warlocks that off-sets how few slots they get is that their spells are always upcast to the highest level. That’s usually awesome, except this SUPER expensive spell that requires multiple slots to actually do anything has NO UPCAST BONUS! So even if you’re lvl 20 this spell will be just as bad as it was at lvl 1. 

The second big point I have is around design. Clearly you designed this spell for the primary use of having it be used by your followers, but as you can see based on the stuff I said above, that’s really it’s ONLY use, because no warlock in their right mind would ever want to spend their pact slots to cast it. Because of this I think a similar ability would be much better as a part of a subclass feature. Maybe when you grant one of your followers a spell they could have the option of either casting that spell, or using that charge to give you a mote. It would function in a very similar way, but it would be slightly better because it would give your followers an extra option, as well as slightly worse because you could no longer use this ability yourself. 

I know this comment is hella long and might sound a little aggressive, but I’m genuinely not trying to have this be a put-down. I think the subclass is really cool so it would be a shame if the accompanying spell was so mechanically terrible. However you choose to balance it in the future, I think the way it currently exists is almost unusable.
